gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tamil-suppleme: Retro and crowded up top. Styro packs its letters nearly shut, while Noto Sans Tamil Supplement opens round, tall-bodied forms like parentheses, so a long page feels stocky and sturdy rather than tight.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tangsa: Commanding, that's Styro, with letters jammed nearly shut. Noto Sans Tangsa has wide, inviting round shapes, so shrinking the heading would lose its punch while the body stays easy.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-thaana: Noto Sans Thaana reads wide and open, with big lowercase forms. Under Styro's crowded retro heading, a long stretch of text feels like stepping out of a tight hallway into daylight.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-thai-looped: Clean and bold-looking, Noto Sans Thai Looped stands tall. Beside Styro's pressed-shut retro letters, a long passage gets spacious curve endings that keep the dense, stocky lowercase from feeling heavy.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-tirhuta: Styro's letters are pressed shut, tight and retro. Noto Sans Tirhuta cuts its terminals back to leave a big gap and stands on a dominant x-height, so a long read stays breezy.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-ugaritic: Tight meets open here. Noto Sans Ugaritic leaves its letter mouths unjoined like a chalk arc, and its small step from lowercase to capitals gives Styro's crowded retro swagger a friendly counterweight.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-vai: Noto Sans Vai forms words as solid blocks rather than skylines, with generous space where curves meet stems. And Styro's retro, jammed-shut letters give those open blocks a commanding headline to sit beneath.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-vithkuqi: Noto Sans Vithkuqi keeps its a, c, e and s open in the throat, with barely any step up to capitals. Under Styro's crowded retro heading, long text moves easily.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-wancho: Noto Sans Wancho is hulking, like thick chalk pressed hard, with a wide gap at the e terminal. Noto Sans Wancho keeps a long stretch of sans-serif text sturdy and open, a clear release from Styro's crowded, retro closeness.
gen-fs-styro-gf-noto-sans-warang-citi: Crowded, retro, and loud. Styro squeezes its letters shut, while Noto Sans Warang Citi sets words as solid blocks with wide channels into each counter, a plain sans that lets the heading's swagger stand out.
